At River AI, our mission is to create personal AI owned and shaped by each individual. To achieve this, we are rewriting the entire stack from scratch: personal hardware for local inference, bespoke training infrastructure, next\-generation UIs, and frontier deep learning research.
   

  

 Who we are
   

  

 We are scientists, engineers, and builders from the industry's top tech companies and AI labs. We bring a proven track record of scaling consumer systems for hundreds of millions of users and architecting the pre\-training infrastructure behind today's frontier models.
   

  

**About The Role**
 We are looking for exceptional inference systems engineers to build the engines that serve large models through the River API. Your goal is to deliver fast, reliable inference while making efficient use of GPU compute and memory.
   

  

 You will take ownership of the serving runtime, from request scheduling and continuous batching to KV\-cache management, distributed model execution, and checkpoint loading. Your work will support both customer\-facing inference and the sampling workloads that power reinforcement learning.
   

  

 Working closely with GPU kernel engineers, researchers, and infrastructure engineers, you will bring new models into production and improve their performance across realistic workloads. You will measure success through latency, throughput, reliability, and cost, with careful attention to numerical correctness and model behavior.
   

  

**What You’ll Do**
* Optimize inference for dense and mixture\-of\-experts models, including fine\-tuned models and adapters.
* Improve batching, caching, and admission control to balance throughput, latency, memory use, and fairness.
* Accelerate multi\-GPU execution, communication, and model loading while preserving model\-version consistency.
* Improve RL sampling throughput while keeping samples and log probabilities tied to the correct model version.
* Build reliable streaming, cancellation, and recovery under failures and overload.
* Profile bottlenecks and validate improvements through reproducible performance and correctness tests.


**Skills \& Qualifications**
**Minimum Qualifications:**
* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
* Experience building inference engines or performance\-sensitive distributed services.
* Strong understanding of transformer inference, GPU memory, concurrency, and networking.
* Proficiency in Python and C\+\+ or Rust.
* Strong debugging and profiling skills across models, runtimes, and services.
* A collaborative mindset and strong ownership of engineering outcomes.


**Preferred Qualifications:** 
*(We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet all of these)*
* Experience extending SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT\-LLM, or similar frameworks.
* Work on advanced serving techniques, such as speculative decoding or disaggregated prefill and decode.
* Familiarity with expert parallelism, GPU collectives, and quantized inference.
* Experience with multi\-adapter serving, dynamic checkpoint loading, or RL sampling.
* Familiarity with CUDA graphs, custom kernels, and NVIDIA profiling tools.
* Experience operating model\-serving systems under production traffic.


**Logistics \& Benefits**

* Compensation: $200,000–$420,000 USD annual base pay, depending on experience and skills, plus equity.
* Benefits: Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance; unlimited PTO; and relocation assistance as needed.
* Visa Sponsorship: We sponsor visas and support the process for the right candidate.

Role Overview
ID.me is seeking a Software Engineer II to join the Developer Portal team, where we're building the self-service platform that enables organizations to rapidly integrate ID.me.
Identity proofing is fundamentally complex. Integrating an identity proofing flow requires many steps while meeting standards-body assurance requirements. The Developer Portal is the product that brings those pieces together for the external developer.
Today, much of that onboarding is still performed manually by in-house Solutions Consultants who have many other responsibilities. Our mission is to enable customers and their developers to register their application, configure their identity needs, test in a production-like sandbox, and launch to production, all through a modern self-service experience.
This is an early-career role for engineers who are 0 to 2 years into their career and write excellent code. You don't need years of industry experience. You need strong fundamentals, a track record of building real things, and an AI-native way of working: you already use AI coding tools as a core part of how you design, build, test, and debug, and you have the judgment to know when their output is right and when it isn't.
This is a backend-leaning full-stack role . You'll work on the services, APIs, and data models behind the portal (application registration, authorization, and the developer-facing APIs our customers integrate against), and you'll ship the user-facing surfaces those services power in our Next.js and React frontend. You'll start with well-scoped features alongside senior engineers and grow quickly into owning features end-to-end, from API contract to production.
Our backend services are primarily Java (Spring Boot) alongside legacy Ruby services. The frontend is a micro-frontend platform built with Next.js , React , and TypeScript . You don't need to know all of these on day one. If your fundamentals are strong, we're confident you'll pick up whatever the problem requires.
What You'll Do
Build and Ship Developer Features
Design, implement, test, and deploy Developer Portal capabilities across the stack: backend APIs, database changes, and the frontend experiences customers use. Start with well-defined features and bugs, then take on progressively larger and more ambiguous work as you grow.
Write High-Quality, Well-Tested Code
Write clean, readable, maintainable code with strong test coverage. Participate actively in code review, both getting feedback and giving thoughtful feedback to teammates, including senior engineers.
Build AI-First
Use AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) every day to move faster on implementation, testing, debugging, and understanding unfamiliar code. Help the team find better ways to use these tools, and hold AI-generated code to the same bar as code you wrote by hand.
Learn the Identity Stack
Build hands-on depth in authentication and authorization, including OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, enterprise SSO, multi-tenant access control, and credential management, working with our Wallet, Organizations, and Platform Engineering teams.
Operate What You Ship
Help keep the systems our team owns healthy in production: monitoring, alerting, debugging live issues, and participating in on-call once you're ramped up.
Collaborate and Grow
Work closely with Product, Design, and engineers across teams. Learn to break down problems, write short technical designs, and communicate clearly about tradeoffs and progress. You'll have a dedicated mentor and a clear path toward end-to-end feature ownership.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
0 to 2 years of professional software engineering experience.
Excellent coding skills and strong computer science fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, complexity, and debugging.
Fluency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Java, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Kotlin, C#, Ruby).
Evidence that you build real software: internships, substantial class or team projects, open-source contributions, hackathons, or side projects that other people use.
AI-native development workflow : daily, hands-on use of AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to build and ship software, paired with the ability to critically evaluate AI-generated code for correctness, security, performance, and maintainability, and to explain every line you submit.
Experience building with LLMs or agentic workflows (e.g., using the Claude or OpenAI APIs, MCP, or agent frameworks) in projects or coursework.
Understanding of how web applications work, including HTTP, REST APIs, and relational databases/SQL.
Ability to learn unfamiliar systems quickly through independent research and by working with mentors and subject-matter experts.
Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain what you built, why, and what tradeoffs you made.
Preferred Qualifications
Internship experience building backend services or full-stack web applications.
Experience with Java and Spring Boot, or another backend framework (Rails, Node.js/Express, Django, Go).
Experience with React, TypeScript, or Next.js.
Experience with PostgreSQL or another relational database, including schema design.
Exposure to authentication and authorization concepts such as OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWTs, SSO, or access control models.
Experience building developer tools, APIs, SDKs, or documentation that other developers use.
Experience writing automated tests (unit, integration, or end-to-end with tools like Jest, JUnit, or Playwright).
Familiarity with cloud platforms (GCP, AWS, Azure), containers, or CI/CD pipelines.
Interest in security, identity, fraud prevention, or regulated systems.
What Success Looks Like
First 30 days: Your dev environment is set up, you've shipped your first production change, and you understand how the Developer Portal fits into ID.me's identity platform.
First 90 days: You're independently delivering well-scoped features across backend and frontend, contributing meaningfully to code reviews, and using AI tooling to raise both your speed and your quality bar.
First year: You own a meaningful Developer Portal capability end-to-end, from API contract and data model through production operation, and you're a go-to person for at least one part of the system.
You're Encouraged to Apply
We're not looking for someone who checks every box. If you write great code, learn fast, and are excited about building the tools that let developers integrate trusted identity, we want to hear from you, even if your background doesn't match this description exactly.

Role Overview
ID.me is seeking a Software Development Engineer II to join the Life Hub team, building the SuperApp's life-events experience — the surface that helps members discover and access the government, healthcare, and commercial benefits they are eligible for based on major life moments (turning 65, leaving the military, becoming disabled, and similar events).
This role is full stack: you will help build the data model and application logic that connects a member's self-asserted and verified attributes to eligible life events, use cases, and application resources, working across both backend services (Java, REST APIs) and the React/Next.js experiences members interact with. You will work closely with the team's senior engineers, Product, and Design to turn eligibility rules and use-case definitions into working software, starting with the team's Medicare pilot and expanding into additional life events such as retirement and disability.
This position will work from our Mountain View, CA office five days per week.
Key Responsibilities
Build Life Hub Eligibility Logic: Build and maintain application logic that turns eligibility attributes (self-asserted, or read from the Persons and Profiles APIs) into ranked, eligible life events and use cases for a member.
Implement Use-Case & Eligibility Models: Implement use-case and eligibility JSON models, in partnership with senior engineers and the Developer Portal team, that map application resources, use cases, and eligibility conditions for pilot programs such as Medicare.
Support Discovery & Access Flows: Contribute to discovery and access flows, ensuring discovery remains lenient (showing ineligible life events, sorted appropriately) while access enforcement remains a hard gate tied to resource-level policy.
Integrate with Platform APIs: Integrate with Persons, Profiles, and Developer Portal control-plane APIs for eligibility and access data rather than hardcoding business logic client-side.
Build Member-Facing UI: Build and maintain React/Next.js web experiences for Life Hub, turning discovery and eligibility concepts into working, member-centered UI.
Track Attribute Gaps: Support tracking and documentation of attribute gaps (e.g., residency, disability status, entitlement data) in partnership with the Profile and Persons API teams.
Collaborate with Design and Product: Work closely with Design and Product, and ask insightful questions during planning and refinement, to help shape Life Hub's ontology and roadmap.
Performance, Accessibility & Reliability: Ensure shipped features meet ID.me's standards for performance, accessibility, and cross-browser reliability.
Production Support: Provide production support and maintenance for shipped features, including triaging and resolving incidents and bugs.

0–2 years of professional software engineering experience (or equivalent internship/academic project experience).
Working proficiency in at least one modern backend language (Java preferred) and comfort with REST APIs.
Working experience with a modern frontend framework (React and/or Next.js).
Solid fundamentals in data structures, debugging, and automated testing.
Comfortable working on well-defined tickets with pair programming and consultation from more senior engineers.
Clear written and verbal communication — this role requires close collaboration with Product, Design, and adjacent platform teams (Developer Portal, Persons/Profile API).
AI-native engineering practices — comfortable using AI tooling (e.g., code generation, test coverage, documentation) to accelerate development.
